title: How To Do Contact Improvisation Dance # 1 The point of contact

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher explains theoretical concepts of contact improvisation while demonstrating physically with a partner. He speaks calmly and breaks down movements into clear technical categories like rolling, replacing, and sliding.

lesson_structure.note: Teachers introduce themselves and the topic of contact improvisation.
Demonstrating the point of contact and negotiating pressure.

cues: Maintain the kind of pressure that we like

steps_taught.name: The Point of Contact
steps_taught.description: Establishing contact and negotiating pressure between partners.

steps_taught.name: Rolling the Point
steps_taught.description: Rolling the point of contact across bodies.

steps_taught.name: Replacing the Point
steps_taught.description: Taking another body part to maintain the same pressure.

steps_taught.name: Sliding
steps_taught.description: Sliding along each other to move around.

what_works: Clear categorization of concepts into rolling, replacing, and sliding.
Demonstration with a live partner makes the physical relationship visible.
what_hinders: Lack of closer camera angles to see exact hand and body placements.

quotes.text: Contact improvisation is based on a point of contact.
We can roll the point where we're maintaining contact.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates establishing a point of contact on the partner's forearm.
Teachers demonstrate rolling the point of contact while turning back-to-back.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact contact pressure during the turn

extraction.distinctive_method: Categorizing the interaction mechanics strictly into three operations: rolling, replacing, and sliding.
